Problem and context Good-product yield on the 2170 assembly line was initially about 40%. Before increasing output, we had to distinguish whether losses came from the product, equipment, or inspection. Treating a gauge error as a process defect can lead to the wrong process change; treating a real defect as an inspection issue allows it to recur.
I therefore started by aligning production quantity, inspected quantity, defect categories, downtime, and measurement rules rather than tuning one recipe from a headline yield number.
What I owned Managed the production plan, WIP, defect, and downtime view as the assembly-process lead. Aligned the denominator and defect names used by production, quality, equipment, and development teams. Reviewed MSA and Gage R&R with quality engineers to separate misclassification from actual process defects. Tracked owners and retest dates for jig tolerances, recipes, wear parts, vision, and inspection conditions. Applied confirmed conditions to SOPs, QCP, P-FMEA, inspection criteria, and operator training. What I checked and changed Check Why Action Yield denominator and defect names Prevent departments from comparing different numbers Put production, inspection, retest, and scrap rules in one view Measurement system Avoid counting misclassification as a process defect Reviewed MSA/Gage R&R and separated inspection and process causes Jig and alignment Check tolerance and wear effects on position Refined jig tolerance and replacement/inspection rules Recipes and wear parts Keep setting changes separate from physical wear Changed one variable at a time and retested under the same criteria Vision and inspection Match detection conditions to the actual CTQ Rechecked decision conditions against the quality rule The trial object, inspection method, and acceptance rule were held constant. A change reached the line only after a repeat check supported it.
Result and limits Good-product yield improved from about 40% to 98.7% within the verified scope. The confirmed settings and checks were recorded so different operators and shifts could follow the same baseline. I did not modify MES directly; I documented management-field and Cell Tracking requirements for the responsible system team. The 98.7% figure is a career result for this line, period, and denominator. It is not a third-party recalculation from public raw data or a universal result for every 2170 line. Company drawings, recipes, equipment addresses, customer specifications, and raw quality data remain private.
Public links and next evidence Public links Public material for reviewing project evidence and the live user surface.
Company drawings, recipes, and raw quality records remain private. The article states only my role, verification method, and results that can be supported from the career record.
In an interview I can explain the denominator, the MSA separation, the order of condition changes, and how the results entered standard work. Company records and raw production data will not be made public.

Problem: test success is not execution authority These statements describe different facts:
a model read data; a model recommended an action; local code passed tests; an authorized person approved a bounded action; the same artifact ran in the operating environment; an external effect occurred and was read back. Without that separation, “test PASS” can become “ready to deploy,” recommendation can become order approval, and local state can be mistaken for external effect.
This project adds fewer integrations and instead builds a fail-closed Authority & Evidence Plane that stops when any required fact is absent.
Current public boundary: live orders 0 · external effects 0 · C4 not approved · not operational GO
Why the contracts are separated One approved=true flag cannot explain who approved which action, artifact, risk, and time boundary. The foundation therefore separates:
Decision Envelope: intent, risk, evidence, approval principal, idempotency, expected effect; Release Ownership Inventory: source, generated, and runtime owners with hashes; Source Qualification: authoritative, advisory, and HOLD inputs. Foundation Join permits progression only when approval, artifact, restart, and effect evidence agree.

Problem and context An automatic cycle on one machine does not mean a pilot line is ready. Upstream and downstream interfaces, cycle time, precision, repeatability, sensors, alarms, interlocks, operator safety, and recovery must work together. After product input, measurement variation must also be separated from process variation.
This project covered 13 detailed processes and 11 core systems on an NCM 50Ah prismatic-cell assembly pilot line.
What I owned Prepared FAT/SAT acceptance sheets and checked specifications, intermediate-part tolerances, and acceptance criteria. Managed vendor punch lists, action dates, and retest results. Reviewed process capability (Cpk) separately from the measurement system (Gage R&R). Checked laser, ultrasonic, and resistance welding plus filling through tensile, cross-section, leak, Hi-Pot, IR, and X-ray results. Managed materials, WIP, staffing, and lot history for a 200-cell daily plan. Used and improved an Excel VBA tracking sheet where MES was not yet available. Gage R&R checks variation from the measurement system and operators. They are not one “process index.”

Documented work standards, incoming-evaluation criteria, and production-history rules. These are pilot-production results, not long-term mass-production Cpk or a claim about every machine’s individual capability. Problem: similar questions can produce different administrative outcomes A short question such as “Can I qualify after resigning?” may depend on separation reason, insured periods, documents, job-search activity, an individual notice, and agency review. A website that decides the case can conflict with current law or the actual disposition.
The service is therefore a static verification aid, not an eligibility chatbot. It helps a user find:
the closest question type; facts and documents to check; the relevant Work24, ministry, or statute source; what to confirm through an individual notice or competent employment center. Why 165 questions become eight categories Publishing raw conversations would expose personal context and create duplicates. One giant FAQ would make discovery difficult.
The pipeline de-identifies 165 questions, groups them into eight categories by intent and verification requirement, and connects repeated questions to guides and search terms. The completed snapshot includes nine practical guides and 21 search pages.

Problem: executable training code is not yet a reproducible experiment Deep Learning Modeling Textbook is a personal learning and practical validation project for organizing data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and reproducibility as one traceable workflow. Instead of stopping at isolated tutorial code, the project defines a modeling standard that can be reused when new data arrives: frame the problem, run a controlled experiment, and explain the result.
The public repository currently exposes only limited implementation detail. This case study is therefore a design document based on the repository’s stated scope of preprocessing, training, evaluation, and reproducibility management. It does not claim a particular dataset size, model accuracy, completed training run, or production deployment. The directory structure and validation items below are target design criteria, not a list of finished features.
Background: Executable Code Is Not Yet a Trustworthy Experiment A deep-learning example can load data, train a model, and print an accuracy score in a single notebook. In engineering work, however, that output is useful only if the team can answer questions such as:
Which version of the data was used for training? Were training, validation, and test samples kept independent? Was the same preprocessing contract used during training and inference? Which baseline and metric justify the claim that the model improved? Can another run with the same settings reproduce a comparable conclusion? In a manufacturing application, which is more costly: a missed defect or a false alarm? The project treats these questions as part of the experiment itself, not documentation added after training. The primary goal is not to build the most complex network. It is to develop an experimental discipline that preserves the causal chain between data, configuration, code, and results.
Project Goals Separate preprocessing, training, and evaluation into explicit stages. Prevent data leakage and evaluation contamination before model selection. Record configuration, code, environment, and outputs together so experiments can be repeated. Interpret error types and business costs in addition to aggregate accuracy. Create a transfer framework from educational examples to manufacturing quality and equipment data. Why the project uses a pipeline Deep-learning modeling is not one action called “training.” Each stage needs a clear input, output, and responsibility so that a failure can be localized. For that reason, the project models the path from source data to evaluation report as a feedback pipeline.
graph LRA["Raw Data"] --> B["Schema and Quality Checks"]B --> C["Train / Validation / Test Split"]C --> D["Preprocessing and Feature Transformation"]D --> E["Baseline Model"]E --> F["Deep-Learning Training"]F --> G["Fixed-Test Evaluation"]G --> H["Error Analysis"]H --> I["Model, Configuration, and Evaluation Records"]I -->|"Improvement hypothesis"| BThis design was chosen for three practical reasons:
Leakage prevention: the split is fixed first, and preprocessing parameters are fitted only on training data. Comparable experiments: different model architectures use the same split and evaluation functions. Root-cause traceability: a performance change can be connected to data, preprocessing, architecture, or threshold decisions. A notebook is useful for exploration, but its hidden state and cell execution order can make results fragile. Moving repeatable preparation, training, and evaluation logic into functions or scripts creates an explicit execution contract and makes a later transition to production easier.
Architecture and data flow The project separates the data contract, preprocessing, training, evaluation, artifacts, and runtime record so the same configuration can be replayed. A result is not treated as current when its input data or evaluation contract has changed.
Technologies and Why They Were Chosen Python Python provides one language for data handling, model experiments, and evaluation automation. The learning focus is not memorizing one framework’s API. It is understanding the contracts between tensor shapes, data loaders, training loops, loss functions, and evaluation functions so the same reasoning can transfer across frameworks.
Deep-Learning Modeling The model is treated as one component of the problem-solving system. A simple rule or small baseline, a defensible split, and explicit error costs are defined before adding depth or parameters. This order makes it possible to determine whether added model complexity creates real value.
Experiment Management from an MLOps Perspective MLOps here does not mean that a large-scale deployment platform has already been built. It means applying operational discipline during training by recording:
a data snapshot or data-version identifier; train, validation, and test split rules; preprocessing settings and model hyperparameters; random seeds and the execution environment; model weights, evaluation metrics, and error-analysis outputs; and the relationship between a code commit and an experiment result. GitHub GitHub is used to version code and documentation and to preserve why the design changed. The current public repository alone is not sufficient to verify full experimental reproducibility; code, configuration, dependencies, and execution instructions still need to be expanded.
Recommended Repository Structure and Design Rationale The following layout is a target architecture for developing the repository into a reproducible learning and validation system. It does not describe the current implementation as complete.
Deep_Learning_Text_book/ ├─ README.md # Problem definition, run order, result interpretation ├─ configs/ # Data, model, and training configuration ├─ notebooks/ # Exploration and concept validation ├─ src/ │ ├─ data/ # Loading, validation, and splitting │ ├─ preprocessing/ # Shared training/inference transformations │ ├─ models/ # Model construction interfaces │ ├─ train.py # Training entry point │ └─ evaluate.py # Fixed evaluation entry point ├─ tests/ # Schema and preprocessing unit tests ├─ reports/ # Metrics, confusion matrices, and error cases └─ artifacts/ # Models and execution metadata Why Separate notebooks/ from src/ Notebooks are appropriate for inspecting distributions and testing a hypothesis quickly. Reusable preprocessing and training logic should then move into deterministic code with a fixed execution order. This separation reduces dependence on hidden notebook state without sacrificing fast exploration.
Why Keep configs/ Separate When learning rate, batch size, input dimensions, and other settings are scattered throughout code, it becomes difficult to explain which change affected a result. Keeping configuration separate and saving it alongside outputs makes experiment-to-experiment differences inspectable. This case study intentionally does not prescribe “best” values; they must be selected from the data and validation evidence.
Why Separate reports/ from artifacts/ Reports contain evidence for human review, such as metrics and representative errors. Artifacts contain reusable machine outputs, such as model weights and execution metadata. The separation clarifies what should be reviewed, what can be reloaded, and what must be retained for traceability.
Data and Implementation Flow Define the Prediction and Evaluation Unit First Before selecting a model, define what one prediction represents: one image, multiple views of one product, or a time window from a machine. This choice determines the correct split and evaluation method. For manufacturing work, the definition should also state the cost of a missed defect, a false rejection, and delayed inference.
Preserve Raw Data and Validate the Schema Raw data remains immutable and is treated as a read-only reference. File paths, labels, equipment IDs, production dates, lots, and other metadata are checked for format, missing values, and duplicates. A metadata defect can mix samples incorrectly even when the image or sensor values themselves are valid, so schema validation comes before modeling.
Split Before Fitting Preprocessing Computing normalization values from the complete dataset or placing augmented versions of one sample into different sets leaks information. Train, validation, and test boundaries are fixed first; only parameters estimated from the training set are applied to validation and test data.
Manufacturing samples from the same machine, lot, or acquisition session may be highly similar. A random row split can therefore put near-duplicates from the same product into both training and test sets. Depending on the problem, the design evaluates group splits by equipment, lot, or time.
Establish a Simple Baseline A rule-based method or small model is created before introducing a complex network. The baseline is not intended to be the final performer. It is a reference point for determining whether later complexity actually adds measurable value.
Train from Recorded Configuration The data version, split rule, model configuration, training configuration, random seed, and runtime environment are bundled as one experiment record. Training loss is not reviewed in isolation; validation trends and signs of overfitting are recorded as well. The test set remains fixed and is not repeatedly reused for model selection.
Review Metrics Together with Error Cases For classification, accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and the confusion matrix are selected according to operational cost. If passing a defective item is the dominant risk, recall for the defect class and false-negative examples take priority. If excessive false alarms stop production, precision and alarm frequency must be considered as well.
Preserve More Than a Model File Each meaningful result should retain at least the following evidence:
Record Why It Matters Data identifier and split rule Confirms whether the evaluation population changed Code commit and configuration Reconstructs the implementation and conditions Training and validation curves Reveals overfitting, underfitting, or instability Per-class metrics and confusion matrix Exposes error types hidden by averages Representative error samples Produces the next data or model hypothesis Execution environment Explains library and hardware differences Technical Challenges and Resolution Strategy Data Leakage The most dangerous failure is often not model code but a broken evaluation boundary. Duplicate samples, shared lots, common acquisition sessions, or future information must not cross sets. The split rule itself belongs in the configuration and evaluation report so it can be audited.
Class Imbalance Manufacturing quality datasets may contain many normal samples and few rare defects. Overall accuracy can look high even when every item is predicted as normal. The design compares per-class metrics, sampling strategies, loss weighting, and threshold adjustment on a fixed validation set instead of assuming one technique is universally superior.
Reproducibility versus Bit-for-Bit Identity Fixing a random seed does not guarantee identical numbers across hardware and library implementations. Reproducibility is therefore defined as the ability to rerun the same code, data, and settings, reach a comparable conclusion, and explain any variation, rather than requiring every floating-point value to match.
Strong Offline Metrics versus Shop-Floor Performance Lighting, material, sensor, and equipment conditions can differ from the training environment. Offline tests should be supplemented by condition-based slice evaluation, monitoring for change over time, inference-latency checks, and explicit failure handling before a model is considered operationally safe.
Experiment Proliferation When many hyperparameters change at once, it is easy to select only the highest score and lose the causal explanation. The project favors changing one hypothesis at a time and recording unsuccessful experiments as well, preventing the same failed idea from being repeated without context.
AI and human roles AI assists with model candidates, preprocessing and evaluation drafts, experiment-comparison tables, and documentation. A human owns data rights, train-validation-test separation, metrics, runtime identity, result approval, and the publication boundary.

Validation Framework The target validation framework separates data, model, reproducibility, and operations rather than compressing every concern into one score.
Validation Layer Primary Question Example Checks Data Are inputs valid and evaluation boundaries independent? Schema, missing values, duplicates, label distribution, group leakage Model Does the model improve meaningfully over the baseline? Fixed split, per-class metrics, confusion matrix, error cases Reproducibility Can the experiment be explained and rerun? Inference time, out-of-distribution inputs, failure handling, data drift Validation evidence is read according to the decision being made. In quality inspection, a missed defect and a false rejection carry different costs. In equipment anomaly detection, early warning and the operator’s ability to respond can be as important as a classification score.
Resume Relevance: Connecting AI Practice to Manufacturing Engineering Manufacturing root-cause analysis connects process conditions, equipment, material lots, working time, and inspection results. This project applies the same discipline to model development:
Preserve source evidence by separating raw field data from derived data. Control change points by recording code, configuration, and data-split changes as experiment units. Define inspection criteria by connecting model metrics to the cost of accepting a defect or rejecting a good item. Maintain traceability from a model result back to its data version and execution conditions. Analyze causes, not averages by reviewing errors by equipment, lot, time, or operating condition. Standardize repeatable work by documenting the modeling workflow like an engineering work standard. This perspective keeps AI from becoming an isolated research exercise. A model is one element of a manufacturing process; it becomes a useful quality-improvement tool only when data-collection conditions, decision thresholds, traceability, and failure response are designed together. For a resume, the project demonstrates systems thinking and verification discipline rather than claiming an unverified production deployment or headline accuracy figure.
Current Limitations The public repository does not yet expose enough code, data documentation, configuration, or execution results to substantiate the full project scope. No validated performance figures for a specific dataset and model are available, so model rankings or quantitative improvements cannot be claimed. Reproducible commands, dependency versions, and automated tests cannot be verified from the public materials alone. Problem: accuracy alone cannot define a welding-defect operating threshold Item Verified scope Problem Micro-defect features overlapped with normal surfaces, data was imbalanced, and accuracy alone did not represent the cost of passing a defective weld. Role I was responsible for evaluation-metric design and validation, including F1, recall, false-positive behavior, and threshold interpretation. Action The team separated roughly 60,000 AI-Hub images from 198 field images, compared a DenseNet baseline, a two-model combination, and a ResNet+DeiT ensemble, then reviewed a second test set and tuned the decision threshold to prioritize missed-defect control. Result On the recorded evaluation set and selected threshold, the report lists F1 93.10%, Recall 100%, and Precision 87.07%. These values do not establish production-wide generalization. Evidence The public report’s dataset, model-evolution, second-test, threshold, and final-metric slides; no dedicated public repository. Resume bullets Separated approximately 60,000 public welding images and 198 field images by learning/field-validation purpose instead of presenting them as one undifferentiated training set. Compared DenseNet, a two-model combination, and a ResNet+DeiT ensemble, then used second-test error review to tune the operating threshold around missed-defect cost. Recorded F1 93.10%, Recall 100%, and Precision 87.07% on the stated evaluation set and defined manual reinspection as the control for remaining false positives. Interview STAR Situation: Missing a small weld defect carried a higher quality risk than sending a normal part to reinspection, while accuracy could remain high under class imbalance. Task: Establish a comparable evaluation framework and a decision threshold aligned with that asymmetric risk. Action: Separate data sources, compare model stages on the same metrics, inspect mixed normal/defect regions in a second test, and search thresholds that retained recall. Result: The selected evaluation produced Recall 100%, F1 93.10%, and Precision 87.07%. I also documented that this is inspection-assistance evidence, not proof of autonomous production deployment. Why this project was structured this way Manufacturing vision is not finished when a model outputs a class. A deployable quality decision must answer four questions:
What exactly counts as a defect? Which data was used for learning and which data checks field transfer? What is the cost of a false negative versus a false positive? Can a quality engineer review the evidence behind a wrong decision? My battery-assembly experience with laser and ultrasonic welding made the decision boundary the center of this project. The model architecture matters, but the operational threshold and reinspection rule determine how a model affects quality risk.

The useful work was maintaining a common evaluation frame and reviewing where normal and defect predictions overlapped.
Why recall was prioritized For defect probability (p) and threshold (t), lowering (t) normally increases sensitivity but can increase false alarms. The quality tradeoff is summarized by:
[ \text{Precision} = \frac{TP}{TP+FP}, \qquad \text{Recall} = \frac{TP}{TP+FN} ]
[ \text{F1} = 2 \cdot \frac{\text{Precision}\cdot\text{Recall}}{\text{Precision}+\text{Recall}} ]

Problem: process and communication risk must be tested before equipment deployment Item Verified scope Problem Process sequences and parameter assumptions could only be checked late with physical equipment, while PLC, SCADA, and virtual-model data integrity was hard to review in advance. Role In a ten-person team, I worked in the Digital Twin group on AI-model selection/training, communications setup, and technical research. Ladder and SCADA implementation belonged to other team members and is not presented as my individual work. Action I mapped the Factory I/O–PLC–SCADA–OPC UA data path, reviewed the DQN control candidate, and defined the boundary between control, monitoring, and AI-assisted optimization. Result The team integrated process flow, Ladder/Factory I/O, SCADA, web, and AI-extension concepts into one demonstration and report. The cited 50–75% setup reduction and 50% expansion-labor reduction are expected benefits/targets, not measured factory outcomes. Evidence The team report’s R&R table, architecture, result, and expected-benefit slides; no dedicated public source repository. Resume bullets Owned AI-model selection/training and OPC UA communications scope in a ten-person manufacturing-DX project that connected Factory I/O, PLC, SCADA, and a virtual commissioning scenario. Converted battery-line FAT/SAT experience into failure-oriented checks covering missing sensors, communication delay, restart conditions, and safe PLC authority. Kept the report’s 50–75% setup and 50% expansion-effort figures as pre-production targets rather than presenting them as measured plant savings. Interview STAR Situation: High-capital equipment creates late discovery risk because control logic and data integrity are difficult to test before physical trial. Task: My scope was to define where AI and communications fit so that control and monitoring layers used consistent data without giving AI unrestricted equipment authority. Action: I organized the OPC UA data flow, reviewed DQN as an optimization candidate, and kept deterministic control and safety checks inside the PLC boundary. Result: The team produced an integrated simulation and report. Quantified values remained expected benefits until controlled before/after measurement is available. Why the project uses virtual commissioning The project models a Giga Press factory context through four responsibilities:
edge acquisition and signal normalization; PLC sequence, interlock, and safe-state control; SCADA state, alarm, and history visibility; Factory I/O virtual commissioning and fault-scenario checks. It is a team PoC and design scenario. It does not claim that a production Giga Press, its safety PLC, hydraulics, or complete physical dynamics were commissioned.

Edge devices may collect and normalize data, and AI may recommend parameters, but emergency stop, door interlock, sequence permission, and communication-timeout behavior remain deterministic PLC/safety responsibilities.
Technologies and data contract Exposing physical PLC addresses directly to every consumer would make a small I/O change ripple through SCADA and reporting. The scenario therefore uses a logical tag model.
Field Purpose equipment_id Stable equipment identity signal_name Human-readable process signal value Boolean, numeric, or state value quality Good, delayed, disconnected, or invalid timestamp Event ordering and freshness mode Auto, manual, or maintenance state OPC UA is useful when meaning, quality, and hierarchy must be shared upstream. Modbus/TCP remains a simpler candidate for constrained register exchange. The article treats them as interface choices subject to device and system requirements rather than claiming every protocol was production-deployed.
Implementation sequence Define normal process steps together with stop, timeout, and restart conditions. Build an I/O list and a logical tag dictionary. Separate reusable command/status/alarm/interlock blocks from equipment-specific exceptions. Treat communication loss as a quality state and require PLC re-authorization after recovery. Run Factory I/O scenarios for normal cycles, missing completion, duplicate sensors, and delayed actuators. Present process state, alarm cause, and communication freshness together in SCADA. Place AI at the optimization/recommendation boundary, not as an unrestricted safety controller. The problem Manufacturing knowledge is split across process, equipment, quality, defect, and corrective-action documents. As the collection grows, one machine acquires several names, relationships point to missing records, and unsupported explanations enter search results.
HeungTology is not a document-count project. It is a personal project for validating human-edited documents, tracing process and equipment relationships, and showing which source section supports a retrieved answer.
Area Public scope Problem Duplicate identities, broken relationships, weak provenance, and local-path leakage My scope Data structure, transformation and validation, graph representation, and retrieval design Technologies YAML, JSON Schema, JSON-LD, OWL, SHACL, Neo4j, and Python Current status Described only within the code and documentation visible in the public repository Withheld claims Local release counts and completion ratings that cannot be reproduced from a public report Why it is structured this way Keeping authoring, graph exchange, and retrieval data in one hand-maintained file makes drift likely. The project therefore separates their responsibilities.
flowchart LR A["Markdown + YAML\nhuman-edited source"] --> B["Schema, relation, and path checks"] B --> C["JSON-LD / OWL / SHACL\nexchange and semantic checks"] B --> D["Heading-aware retrieval data"] D --> E["Vector + full-text"] C --> F["Neo4j relationship traversal"] E --> G["Rank fusion and reranking"] F --> G G --> H["Answer with source document and heading"] YAML and JSON Schema constrain the fields entered by a person. JSON-LD, OWL, and SHACL handle exchange, semantics, and relationship shapes. Neo4j supports questions that traverse process, equipment, defect, cause, and action. Vector and full-text search cover semantic similarity and exact equipment terms. Citation rules prevent a plausible retrieval result from becoming a confident answer without a source. What I designed and changed Fix the document contract first Each record keeps identity, aliases, classification, lifecycle, provenance, relationships, and supported claims in predictable fields. Duplicate keys, missing relationship targets, local absolute paths, and structural errors are reported before release. Ambiguous relationships remain in a review queue rather than being attached to the nearest-looking record.
Keep retrieval stages explicit Vector and lexical scores are not directly added because they have different scales. Each search produces a ranked candidate list; ranks are fused, selected graph relationships are expanded, and the final context is reranked. Source paths and headings travel with the context so a reviewer can trace the answer.
Correct the publication boundary An earlier version of this article presented local release metrics as though the same report were directly reproducible from the public repository. Because that report is not publicly readable, node, assertion, error, and warning counts have been removed from the public achievement claim. The repository link now supports only what a visitor can inspect there.
Result and manufacturing relevance The project establishes a practical difference between “a document exists” and “a claim has traceable support.” It also keeps knowledge retrieval separate from physical control authority.
The design comes from field experience where process settings, inspection criteria, equipment history, and corrective actions lived in separate documents. The same discipline used to separate criteria and evidence in QCP, P-FMEA, and MSA informs the source, claim, and validation boundaries here.
Evidence and limits The public repository exposes the data structure, transformation and validation code, and retrieval design documentation. Local validation counts that are not reproduced publicly are not used as headline results. The documents do not all have the same depth of human review. Retrieval quality still needs a fixed question set and relevance judgments. Knowledge retrieval must remain a read function, separate from equipment control. The problem A robot program is more than a list of joint positions. Tool and TCP settings, waypoints, motion commands, branches, speed, and I/O fields reference one another. If a PC editor reads only familiar fields and rewrites the file, the result may look correct on screen while failing on the teach pendant.
Communication has a similar ownership problem. If the HMI, historian, and digital twin each open a robot socket, it becomes difficult to identify the command owner and the latest state.
Area Scope Goal Preserve source-JSON references and centralize responsibility for the robot connection My scope JSON compatibility, PC-HMI, communications, history, and twin service boundaries Technologies Python, CustomTkinter, IndyDCP, MQTT, MySQL, WebSocket, and Docker Current status Design and prototype; public link withheld Remaining validation Firmware-specific regression, long reconnect tests, and Omniverse E2E Why the system is divided this way flowchart LR A["Conty JSON"] --> B["Load, inspect, edit, save"] B --> C["Preserve references and unknown fields"] D["PC-HMI"] --> E["Robot Controller\nsingle IndyDCP owner"] E --> F["MQTT command / result / state"] F --> G["DB Worker\njob and error history"] F --> H["PLC Bridge"] F --> I["Read-only Digital Twin"] JSON compatibility Unknown source fields are preserved instead of discarded. The core check is load → edit → save → reload → compare references. Waypoint, program-tree, and motion-command references are inspected separately.
One physical-socket owner Only the Robot Controller owns the IndyDCP connection. The HMI sends requests; the database and twin consume state. This prevents a display or storage failure from silently becoming another physical-control path.
Separate command and state events MQTT command, result, realtime state, connection, and error events have different responsibilities. A command identifier should connect each request with its outcome. Idempotency, authentication, and topic permissions remain required before a production-like connection.
What I built and reviewed A hierarchical JSON browser and editor Parser and serializer boundaries that preserve source data A Robot Controller-centered communications design A DB Worker for job, state, and error history Event contracts shared by PLC and HMI consumers A read-only twin without physical command controls Progressive Offline UI, Direct, and Gateway execution modes The workflow begins without a robot so JSON and screen behavior can be checked first. Direct communication is added next, followed by the gateway and state consumers. This staged path makes failures easier to isolate.
Result The result is not presented as “remote robot control.” The project treats file compatibility and physical-control ownership as one engineering problem. It also keeps HMI, history, and visualization functions from independently owning the control socket.
Evidence and limits The associated repository was reported to contain internal-network, local-path, and default-configuration patterns. Its GitHub and report buttons are withheld until cleanup and a new public review are complete.
This is not claimed as a production deployment. Round-trip behavior still needs broader testing across Indy7 firmware versions. Long-running reconnect and duplicate-command tests with hardware remain open. Omniverse is a future adapter direction, not a completed result. The twin remains an observation layer without physical command authority. Design and validation record Verification details Design and validation record

Problem: controlling career facts matters more than fluent generation resumOpenAI explores a narrower problem than “ask an LLM to write a resume.” It separates verified career facts, private fields, target-role selection, draft generation, and output validation so that polished wording cannot silently alter dates, employers, roles, or measured outcomes.
Area Design Frontend React form and draft review API Flask request validation and generation orchestration Data structured career facts with evidence/status fields LLM controlled prompt and optional adaptation path Safety personal-data minimization and public/private separation QA claim/date/number checks before export Why structure comes before fine-tuning Fine-tuning can make style more consistent, but it cannot repair missing or contradictory facts. The first quality gate is a structured source model.
{ "experience_id": "exp-example", "employer": "verified employer", "period": {"start": "YYYY-MM", "end": "YYYY-MM"}, "role": "verified role", "claims": [ { "statement": "bounded achievement", "evidence": "source reference", "status": "verified", "public": true } ] } Sensitive fields such as address, date of birth, phone number, credentials, or raw company documents should not be sent merely because they exist in a resume file. The public rendering model contains only approved technical facts.
Architecture flowchart LRA["Private source documents"] --> B["Local extraction / normalization"]B --> C["Verified career-fact store"]C --> D["Public-field filter"]D --> E["Target-role evidence selection"]E --> F["Flask generation request"]F --> G["LLM draft"]G --> H["Claim/date/number validation"]H --> I["Human review"]I --> J["Exported draft"]The React layer captures job target and review choices. Flask owns schema validation, field filtering, prompt assembly, and result checks. The LLM receives only the minimum evidence required for the chosen output.
Technologies and implementation The PoC uses React for structured input, Flask for the API boundary, explicit career-evidence records, an LLM for drafting, and output checks for unsupported or sensitive content. Facts and role-specific wording remain separate reviewable layers.
AI and human roles AI proposes role-specific drafts, wording alternatives, and possible omissions. A human owns the source career facts, numeric evidence, privacy and employer-confidentiality review, target-role relevance, and the final submitted text.

Validation design The PoC treats generation as a draft process with deterministic gates.
Every employer, period, role, and number must exist in the source fact store. A claim marked unverified cannot be promoted as achieved. Conflicting date ranges produce a review item instead of an automatic choice. Private fields are removed before the external-model boundary. Unsupported superlatives and invented tools are flagged. Korean and English outputs must point to the same fact IDs. Role-specific selection One fact store can support several views without rewriting history.
Manufacturing engineering: line setup, FAT/SAT, process conditions, yield, quality systems. Manufacturing AI & data: Vision AI, PLC/SCADA/MES, digital twin, data contract, deployment boundary. Data analysis: dataset definition, metric choice, validation, data quality, provenance, decision impact. The application changes ordering and explanation, not the underlying facts.
Current limits The current portfolio does not provide a public repository or evaluation dataset for this PoC. A generated resume still requires human review. Style consistency is not evidence accuracy. Fine-tuning must not include unredacted personal or confidential documents. Quality needs a fixed evaluation set containing contradictions, missing evidence, and sensitive fields. Next steps Publish a sanitized schema and sample dataset. Add claim-level provenance and output-to-source links. Build deterministic tests for dates, numbers, language parity, and privacy filtering. Compare prompt-only, retrieval-assisted, and fine-tuned variants on the same evaluation set. Record user acceptance/edit distance rather than relying only on LLM-style metrics. This case demonstrates an important AI application principle: structured facts, privacy boundaries, and deterministic validation come before fluent generation.
